proxy_language: Proto-Semitic (reconstructed), with Proto-Afroasiatic as a deeper fallback; cultural-linguistic link is speculative
proxy_rationale: Mureybet (c. 10,200-8,500 BCE, Epipaleolithic/Natufian-adjacent to PPNA, Middle Euphrates) is known only archaeologically; no language is attested. Some scholars (Bar-Yosef, Renfrew-style arguments, Militarev, Diakonoff on Afroasiatic) tentatively link Levantine Natufian/PPNA foragers and early farmers with Afroasiatic, and the Middle Euphrates later hosts Semitic (Amorite, Eblaite, Mari Akkadian) speakers, but the 9,000+ year gap makes any Proto-Semitic form a stylistic proxy, not a claim. Proto-Semitic is chosen because it is the best-reconstructed language family historically native to the region and has a transparent root-and-pattern morphology a name builder can use consistently. Names should be treated as evocative reconstructions only.
phonology: Proto-Semitic consonants (Kogan/Huehnergard): stops b p t d t' (emphatic) k g k' ; fricatives s z s' (emphatic affricate/ejective) sh (sin/s-hat) h x gh (voiced velar) h-bar (pharyngeal) ayin; laryngeals ' (glottal stop) and h; sonorants m n l r; glides w y; interdentals th dh th' (emphatic). Vowels: short a i u, long a: i: u:; diphthongs aw ay. No voiced/voiceless contrast beyond reconstruction; emphatics are glottalic/ejective. Stress predictable, not phonemic.
phonotactics: Canonical syllable shapes CV, CVC, CV: (long vowel), no word-initial vowel (words begin with a consonant, often ' glottal stop that is not written in simplified scholarly practice), no initial clusters, no vowel hiatus. Medial CC clusters arise only across syllable boundary (CVC.CV). Word-final is typically a short vowel (case ending -u/-i/-a in nouns) or a consonant after case loss. Roots are triconsonantal (occasionally biconsonantal); the vowels and affixes fill a template.
orthography: Use conventional Semitist transliteration simplified to Latin letters: b p t d k g q (emphatic k) ' (glottal stop) ' for ayin written as ` if needed but avoid in game, h, kh/x, gh, sh (for s-hat), s, z, th, dh, m, n, l, r, w, y, plus emphatics rendered with an apostrophe after the consonant (t' s' q written q). Vowels a i u with macron or doubled vowel for length (aa ii uu). Reconstructed forms carry asterisk in glosses but not in the game names themselves.
morphology: Root-and-pattern (templatic) system: triconsonantal root + vocalic pattern gives noun/verb meaning, e.g. *k-t-b 'write'. Nouns inflect for gender (masc, fem -at), number (sg, dual -aan/-ayn, pl -uu/-aat or broken plural), and three cases (nominative -u, genitive -i, accusative -a), plus definiteness added later. Common noun patterns: CaCC (qatl), CiCaaC, CuCuuC, maCCaC (place noun), maCCaCat (instrument/place), taCCuCat (abstract). Prefix ma- forms place/instrument nouns; suffix -at feminine/abstract; prefix sha- causative; prefix mu- agent participle.
compounding: Compounding is not productive; construct state (genitive chain) is the standard way to express 'X of Y': head noun in construct state (case ending dropped or -u bound form) followed by the dependent noun in genitive: bayt-u 'house of' + X-i. 'X-maker' formed with agent participle mu-CaCCiC + object in genitive or an agent noun CaCCaC (e.g. *haddaad 'smith' pattern). Name builder: head + genitive dependent, optionally with attributive adjective after the noun.
noun_phrase_order: Head-initial. Noun + genitive possessor (construct); noun + adjective (adjective agrees in gender, number, case and definiteness); demonstratives may precede or follow; numerals precede the noun for 1-2 and are nominal for higher numbers. Example: *bayt-u shamsh-i 'house of the sun'.

notes: The Mureybetian language is entirely unknown; Proto-Semitic is a speculative stylistic proxy only. Avoid claiming genetic linkage. Keep names as templatic noun forms: CV(C)CV(C) with no initial vowels, no clusters at word start, optional case ending -u/-i/-a, feminine -at, and construct chains for compounds. The current game strings (e.g. Ghizagha ma'ig, Cuc'ac citsic) use letters like c and ts that do not belong to this system and should be replaced. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word since this is not a Goidelic language.
